text: dsh-plugin-mermaid 是一个 DSH Web 插件，会把聊天回复中的 Mermaid 代码块绘制成图表。它在代码块内容区域添加图表界面，并在源码稳定后渲染，因此流式回复中无需等待整条消息结束。用户可以切换图表与源码视图，在图表视图复制图片，在源码视图复制 Mermaid 文本；图表颜色跟随当前主题。插件由 Host 提供本地 Mermaid 运行时资源路由，浏览器端负责识别和绘制图表，适合在 DSH 聊天中直接查看流程图等 Mermaid 内容。需要 DSH Web UI 和插件依赖中的 Mermaid 运行时，无需额外 API 密钥。

dsh-plugin-mermaid renders Mermaid code blocks in DSH Web chat as diagrams, even during streaming replies. Users can switch between diagram and source, copy an image or Mermaid text, and view colors that follow the theme. The Host serves the runtime locally; no API key is needed.
想让聊天里的 Mermaid 代码直接显示成图。
回复还在生成时，能不能先看到已经写完的流程图？
Show Mermaid diagrams inline in chat instead of leaving them as code.
dsh-plugin-mermaid 的功能「聊天图表渲染」：识别代码块中的 Mermaid 图表语法，并在原代码块内显示渲染结果。来源稳定后自动绘制，渲染失败时保留原代码内容。
dsh-plugin-mermaid 的功能「图表与源码复制」：界面提供图表和源码视图切换；图表视图可复制渲染图片，源码视图可复制 Mermaid 文本。

mermaid 代码块画成图表，边流式输出边画

中文说明（点开） —— 不用等一轮回复结束才看到图

dsh-plugin-mermaid README · dsh-plugin-mermaid：**它是什么**：模型在回复里写 ```` ```mermaid ```` 围栏，你看到的是图，不是代码。图上方一条细栏写着 `Mermaid`，右边是 **复制** 和 **源码/图表** 开关。

**为什么不是"等回复结束再画"**：DSH 渲染流式回复时，**已完成的块只解析一次、React 元素被缓存**，每个 token 只重建尾部那一块。所以规则只有一条：**源文本静止 220ms 才画**。token 在流 → 计时器一直被重置 → 什么都不画；围栏一闭、后面的正文开始到达 → 块冻结 → 图立刻出现。模型在围栏里停顿时不会画出半张图。

**复制**：图模式复制一张 PNG（2–3 倍尺寸、铺了代码块自己的底色，粘到文档里就是一张图）；源码模式复制 Mermaid 文本。浏览器剪贴板不收 SVG，所以图是先栅格化再写的 —— 这也是 Mermaid 跑在 `htmlLabels: false` 的原因：`<foreignObject>` 里的 HTML 在"SVG 当图片"时会消失。

**认不出来就不画**：Mermaid 解析失败的块原样保留，不插任何东西。

dsh-plugin-mermaid README · dsh-plugin-mermaid：**装法**：Plugin Manager 的 Add plugin 填 `github:kjx-talesofai/dsh-plugin-mermaid#v0.2.1`，或指向本地目录。装完**重启 app**（Host 半边开机才加载资产路由），页面再 **⌘R**。

**它没有做什么**：不改 Markdown 渲染器、不占槽位、不加工具。只在代码块的 `data-code-block-content` 里加一个节点，用一条 `:has()` 规则把源码 `<pre>` 藏起来。

</details>

dsh-plugin-mermaid README · What it does：The model writes a fenced block:

````text
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["工作区"] --> B["暂存区"] --> C["仓库"]
```
````

You see the diagram, under a small bar that names it and offers **源码**
(source) and copy. The block's own "Code block" banner is hidden while the
diagram is shown, because the plugin never touches the `<pre>` React owns — it
adds a sibling and hides the original with CSS.

dsh-plugin-mermaid README · What it does：**Copy follows the view.** With the diagram on screen the button puts a PNG on
the clipboard (2–3× the drawn size, on the block's own surface colour, so it
pastes into a document without a transparent-background surprise); with the
source on screen it copies the Mermaid text. Browser clipboards will not take an
SVG reliably, so the diagram is drawn through a canvas first — which is also why
Mermaid runs with `htmlLabels: false`: `foreignObject` HTML does not survive that
trip.

dsh-plugin-mermaid README · Why this is not a Markdown plugin：There is no slot between "Markdown" and "code block". The only seat a plugin can
take is the whole `assistant-step` node, and taking it would mean re-implementing
Markdown — file links, image lightboxes, KaTeX, syntax highlighting, copy
buttons, sticky banners — to add one block type.

So the plugin decorates the primitive's own markup instead:

The coupling is that markup. `tests/dom.test.mjs` drives a stand-in with the same
shape in a real browser, so a change to it fails loudly here instead of silently
drawing nothing.
section: Why this is not a Markdown plugin

text:
dsh-plugin-mermaid README · Why streaming needs care：DSH renders a live reply with an incremental Markdown renderer: every completed
block is parsed once and its React elements are cached, so only the growing tail
is re-rendered on each token. That gives one precise rule:

> never draw the tail; draw only a source that has stopped changing.

dsh-plugin-mermaid README · Why streaming needs care：A block is drawn after its source has been unchanged for 220 ms. While tokens
flow the timer keeps resetting; when the fence closes and the next prose starts,
the block freezes, and the diagram appears mid-reply — no waiting for the turn to
end. A pause *inside* an open fence that lasts longer than 220 ms will draw
whatever has arrived; if the source then keeps growing, the panel is dropped and
redrawn, and a source Mermaid rejects leaves the code block exactly as it was.

dsh-plugin-mermaid README · Why streaming needs care：Rendered diagrams are cached by source + theme, so a re-render (React rebuilding
the message, a theme switch) costs no Mermaid work.

dsh-plugin-mermaid README · Where Mermaid comes from：The browser half asks the Host for `/api/mermaid.asset.js`; the Host serves the
`mermaid.min.js` from this package's own dependency tree over the same
authenticated, same-origin channel as the rest of the Web UI. The build is found
by Node's own resolution (`createRequire`), not by a fixed
`./node_modules/…` path: pnpm — which the Plugin Manager uses — keeps a
package's dependencies *beside* it, so a fixed path would 404 on every install
from Git while working perfectly in a linked checkout. It is a 3.4 MB
script, so it is fetched the first time a diagram is seen, not on every page
load, and revalidated with an ETag.

dsh-plugin-mermaid README · Limits：- Diagrams are rendered in the browser only. A DSH client without the plugin (a
  phone on an old tab, `--no-client` tooling) shows the code block.
- Mermaid's `strict` security level is used: HTML labels are sanitized, and
  click-to-activate links are not available.
- A diagram Mermaid rejects is not decorated at all. The reason is logged to the
  browser console (`[mermaid] …`); there is no inline error row, because during
  streaming an incomplete diagram would flash one.
- No per-block history: the panel is a view of the file's Markdown, not a record.

dsh-plugin-mermaid README · Install：Use DSH's own **Add plugin** dialog. No npm account, no publishing.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| GitHub | `github:kjx-talesofai/dsh-plugin-mermaid#v0.2.1` |
| Local directory | an absolute path, e.g. `/path/to/dsh-plugin-mermaid` |

Restart the desktop app afterwards: the Host half owns the asset route and is
only loaded at startup. The browser half reloads with the page (`⌘R`).

dsh-plugin-mermaid README · Install：This plugin is **not published to npm**, and `npm install` is not the install
path. Its one runtime dependency (the Mermaid build the Host serves) is installed
from the repository's `package.json`.

dsh-plugin-mermaid README · Tests：```bash
npm ci
npm test           # 18: classifier, loader contract, patch/manifest consistency, the Host route, module resolution
npm run test:dom   # 33 in headless Chrome over CDP: `:has()`, real Mermaid output, the streaming sequence, both clipboard flavours
```

`test:dom` skips when no Chrome or Chromium is installed.
